intended_object: The augmentation homomorphism GLₙ(ℤ ⋉ I) → GLₙ(ℤ), for a two-sided ideal I of a ring R. It applies the augmentation ℤ ⊕ I → ℤ, (z, i) ↦ z, to every entry. Its kernel is Milnor's GLₙ(I) from algebraic K-theory. This reading comes from the docstring, the module documentation and how the next definition, `idealGeneralLinearGroup`, uses it.
explanation:
The body is `mapRingHom` (the map induced on GLₙ by a ring homomorphism) applied to `Unitization.fstHom` over ℤ. `Unitization.fstHom` is exactly the augmentation ℤ ⊕ I → ℤ that keeps the integer part, so the definition gives the entrywise augmentation of invertible matrices over the unitization, which is the standard map. Using ℤ as the base ring of the unitization is the standard choice for defining GL(I) of a non-unital ring or ideal, as in Milnor and Weibel. The index type n is any finite type with decidable equality.

The body never uses the ambient ring R, only I viewed as a non-unital ring. So the construction would also make sense for any non-unital ring A, giving GLₙ(Unitization ℤ A) → GLₙ(ℤ). The library, however, names and documents it as the augmentation attached to an ideal and uses it only to compare with congruence subgroups of R. Defining it for two-sided ideals matches how the literature presents GL(I), so I don't count this as too narrow.

Mathlib has no dedicated declaration for this augmentation. It is the composite of the general `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.mapRingHom` and `Unitization.fstHom`, which the definition uses directly. There are no edge-case problems: if I = 0, the map is an isomorphism GLₙ(ℤ) ≅ GLₙ(ℤ), as it should be.
